content.text: Jira can restrict an issue to a security level. The mirror has no column for it, so nothing downstream can tell.

Measured: internal/sync/sync.go:43-48 baseFields does not request security; fields.security is NULL across both the demo snapshot and the oss mirror; there is no security column in the schema. Cloud's create-issue reference documents "security": {"id": "10000"} as a first-class field.

The exposure is bounded: an issue the credential cannot see never enters the mirror at all, so this is not a way to read restricted work. What it is: an issue that IS restricted and IS visible to this credential appears indistinguishable from a public one, so an agent can quote it into a commit message, a chat, or a public summary without ever being told it was marked sensitive. Same family as the comment-visibility defect.

Fix shape: a security_level_id column (id, not the display name — the localization trap), surfaced in `gadak issue` and available to SQL, plus a line in the agent skill about checking it before quoting an issue anywhere public.
Medium rather than High because neither dogfood site uses security levels, so this is unverified against real data; the absence of the column is confirmed in code.
Found by the Jira-surface gap sweep (track C, score 7/10).
